BRACE and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications

This page maps each risk in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications for 2026 to BRACE controls (C1–C9) and items in the BRACE sign-off checklist. The list comes from the OWASP GenAI Security Project. Its resource page gives a release date of 9 December 2025. The IDs and names below were copied from the official list page on 2026-11-24.

How to read this mappingSummaryMappingGapsLimits

How to read this mapping

  • Direct — passing the listed BRACE items prevents the risk or contains its damage in a deployed agent.
  • Partial — the listed items reduce the risk or help detect it, but some of it is left to other work.
  • Out of scope — BRACE doesn't address it; the row says why in a few words.

Item IDs refer to the checklist, most relevant first. An item counts only when its result is Pass. Passing an item is not proof that a risk is gone. Test it with the verification recipes.

Mapping

OWASP IDRiskCoverageBRACE controlsBRACE itemsHow BRACE addresses it
ASI01Agent Goal HijackPartialC5, C4, C7Run-time rule 2, Run-time rule 1, Build-time rule 5, Build-time rule 6, Run-time rule 9, Build-time rule 12BRACE assumes some injections will work. Run-time rule 2 tests that a hijacked goal still can't cause harm, and Build-time rule 5 and Build-time rule 6 stop destructive actions without approval. It can't stop the model from being steered in the first place.
ASI02Tool Misuse and ExploitationDirectC4, C5Build-time rule 1, Build-time rule 5, Build-time rule 7, Ecosystem rule 6, Ecosystem rule 4, Ecosystem rule 5, Run-time rule 9The harness allows only needed tools and arguments, sets budgets, and blocks destructive calls. The gateway enforces the same rules at the boundary. Run-time rule 9 catches misuse spread across allowed steps.
ASI03Identity and Privilege AbuseDirectC2Agent rule 1, Build-time rule 2, Build-time rule 3, Build-time rule 4, Ecosystem rule 8, Agent rule 4, Ecosystem rule 6Each agent has its own identity and short-lived, narrow tokens. Ecosystem rule 8 stops delegated authority from growing as it passes between agents. Build-time rule 4 can cut off the agent without cutting off its user.
ASI04Agentic Supply Chain VulnerabilitiesDirectC3, C5Ecosystem rule 2, Ecosystem rule 3, Ecosystem rule 5, Build-time rule 10, Configuration rule 5, Configuration rule 1, Ecosystem rule 4Dependencies, images, models, and tools are vetted, pinned, and listed in the release manifest. Tools are re-checked each time they load, so a changed tool is caught.
ASI05Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)DirectC3, C1, C4Build-time rule 11, Build-time rule 8, Build-time rule 9, Build-time rule 1, Build-time rule 5, Run-time rule 1Code runs in a minimal, isolated runtime, with a stronger sandbox for untrusted code. Network limits keep a breakout from reaching much. BRACE does not find bugs in the code itself.
ASI06Memory & Context PoisoningPartialC6, C5Run-time rule 5, Run-time rule 6, Run-time rule 4, Run-time rule 2Memory is split by tenant and agent, writes are checked, and each entry records where it came from. Run-time rule 5 and Run-time rule 6 are Detection items, required only at higher stakes. Checks on writes can't spot every poisoned fact.
ASI07Insecure Inter-Agent CommunicationPartialC2, C5, C9Ecosystem rule 7, Ecosystem rule 6, Agent rule 4, Ecosystem rule 10, Ecosystem rule 8Messages from peer agents are treated as untrusted and sent through an authenticating gateway, and the audit trail follows calls across services. BRACE does not set a message protocol, encryption, or replay rules.
ASI08Cascading FailuresPartialC8, C4, C7Ecosystem rule 9, Build-time rule 7, Run-time rule 11, Run-time rule 12, Ecosystem rule 12, Configuration rule 7Budgets cap runaway work, and a tested kill switch stops an agent and all its sub-agents in a safe state. Fleet response and rollback limit spread. BRACE does not test how errors flow through a whole multi-agent system.
ASI09Human-Agent Trust ExploitationPartialC4Build-time rule 6, Build-time rule 5Approvals show the reviewer the exact action, so a persuasive summary can't hide it. BRACE does not measure over-trust, social engineering of users, or how the agent presents itself.
ASI10Rogue AgentsPartialC7, C8, C1–C9Run-time rule 10, Run-time rule 8, Run-time rule 9, Run-time rule 11, Ecosystem rule 9, Configuration rule 3, Configuration rule 4, Agent rule 5BRACE watches for misaligned behavior and drift, and can stop a rogue agent and its sub-agents. Isolation and least privilege limit the damage. Run-time rule 8–Run-time rule 10 are Detection items, and no check proves an agent is aligned.

Gaps

  • Steering the model. BRACE limits what a hijacked or rogue agent can do. It does not stop the model from being misled (ASI01, ASI10).
  • Inter-agent protocol security. BRACE has no rule for message signing, encryption, or replay protection between agents (ASI07).
  • System-wide failure testing. BRACE stops and rolls back agents but does not test how one fault spreads through many agents (ASI08).
  • Human factors. BRACE does not cover user training, over-reliance, or deceptive agent output beyond the approval screen (ASI09).
  • Detection items. Several rows depend on Detection items (Run-time rule 5, Run-time rule 6, Run-time rule 8–Run-time rule 10, Ecosystem rule 12). These are required only at higher stakes and autonomy ratings. At lower ratings those rows give less protection.

Limits

  • This mapping is BRACE's judgment. OWASP has not reviewed or endorsed it.
  • Each OWASP risk covers many attack paths. "Direct" means BRACE addresses the main paths for one deployed agent. It does not mean every example in the OWASP text is blocked.
  • Only items with a Pass result count. A Gap, an accepted risk, or an N/A gives no coverage.
  • The OWASP mitigation lists for each risk are not mapped one by one.
  • Recheck this mapping when OWASP publishes a new edition. Last checked 2026-11-24.
